subject: help: N-mixture model, informative priors on detection

messages.subject: help: N-mixture model, informative priors on detection
parts:
Hi all,

In OpenBUGS (using R2OpenBUGS - although I've tried debugging directly in OpenBUGS as well) I get error: "something went wrong in procedure Poisson in module MathRandnum". I am trying to model wetland selection by migrating shorebirds. Most wetlands have 2 surveys (some 3, some 1), however the abundance of shorebirds is highly dynamic and shorebirds turnover between surveys. Thus, I put survey date (julian.z) as a covariate on abundance. Also, many 0's in the data (thus zero-inflation in model) and the data holds little information to derive detection estimates. Thus, I use estimates on detection from another study as informative priors on p (by vegetation class, i.e., light vegetative cover, medium cover, and heavy cover). Also, surveys of wetlands are spatially grouped in townships, thus the zero-inflation model and abundance model have a random effect term for township. I am wondering if anyone can spot the error (I've been debugging this for a while, but am pretty limited in my skills with this type of model and seem to be at that limit) and any help would be much appreciated! 

Also, the ymult matrix deals with na's in the y matrix for wetland reps with missing surveys. Na's in the y matrix are 0's in the ymult matrix, creating p effective (p.eff) of 0. 

BUGS model and full data are attached.

Example of the y data 
237 0  0 NA
238 0  0 NA
239 0  0 NA
240 0  0 NA
241 0  0 NA
242 0  0 NA
243 0  0 NA
244 0 NA NA
245 0  0 NA
246 0 NA NA
247 0 NA NA
248 2  0 NA

load("datax.Nmix.RData")
library(R2OpenBUGS)

sink("BUGS\\zip.Nmix.modelOnP.txt")
cat("
    model{

    #priors for zero-inflation
    a~dnorm(0, 0.44)
    
    # priors for poisson model
    for(k in 1:6){ 
    b[k]~dnorm(0, 0.01)
    }
   
    #priors for detection model
    d.int~dnorm(0,0.44)
    d[1]<-logit(mean.d1)
    mean.d1 ~dbeta(12.3,3.27)
    d[2]<-logit(mean.d2)
    mean.d2 ~dbeta(12,12)
    d[3]<-logit(mean.d3)
    mean.d3 ~dbeta(9.9,89.1)
    
    # random effects
    for(j in 1:nTC){
    rz1[j]~dnorm(0, 1)
    ry1[j]~dnorm(0, 1)
    }
       
    sigmaz1~dunif(0, 12) 
    sigmay1~dunif(0, 12) 
    sigmaeps~dunif(0, 12)
    
    for(w in 1:nW){   #loop over wetlands
    
    #zero-inflation
    z[w]~dbern(pz[w])  
    logit(pz[w]) <- a + sigmaz1*rz1[TC[w]]
     eps[w] ~ dnorm(0,1)
    
    for(t in 1:T){ #loop over the reps within each site/wetland

    N[w,t]~dpois(mu[w,t])
    mu[w,t]<- (1-z[w])*lambda[w,t]
    lambda[w,t] <- exp(max(min(eta[w,t],50),-10))
    eta[w,t] <- b[1] + b[2]*crop.z[w] + b[3]*julian.z[w,t] + b[4]*pow(julian.z[w,t],2) + b[5]*pow(julian.z[w,t],3) + b[6]*peri.l.z[w,t] + sigmay1*ry1[TC[w]] + sigmaeps*eps[w] 
    
    y[w,t]~dbin(p.eff[w,t],N[w,t])
    p.eff[w,t] <- (p[w,t])*(y.mult[w,t])
    logit(p[w,t]) <- d.int + d[1]*veg.1[w,t]+ d[2]*veg.2[w,t] + d[3]*veg.3[w,t] 
    }#
    }
    } #model
    ",fill = TRUE)
sink()

bugsworkingdir <- file.path(getwd(), "BUGS")

parameters <- c("a", "b","d","sigmaz1","sigmay1","sigmaeps") 

inits <- function() list(a=runif(1, -1, 1), b=runif(6, -1, 1),
                         sigmaz1=runif(1, 0.5, 2), sigmay1=runif(1, 0.5, 2),
                         z=as.numeric(rowSums(datax$y,na.rm=T)==0),N=datax$y+1)
mod.zip.Nmix <- bugs(datax, inits= inits, parameters,
             model.file="zip.Nmix.modelOnP.txt", n.chains=2, n.iter=100, 
             n.burnin=2, n.thin=1, debug=TRUE,
             working.directory=bugsworkingdir)


**datax structure: note, peri.l.z is the shoreline length (=survey length, logged and scaled) and crop.z is the proportion of cropland in the township (scaled), TC is the township

parts:
Dear Valerie,

 

Have you had these problems with (much) simpler versions of this model ? Did the Null model run (i.e., where there is an intercept only for the zero-inflation and abundance parts) ? Remember rule # 1: start with a simple model and make it more complex progressively.

 

Also, it is a good idea to throw a problem at two or more of the available BUGS software, i.e., in your case, also WinBUGS and JAGS. Sometimes a model runs in one and not the other and in the very least, the error messages may be complementary.

 

Best regards  -- Marc

parts:
Dear Marc,

Thanks much for the response.

I had the model without the detection component running (i.e. the zero-inflation binomial model and the poisson model). I actually finally had success getting the full model to run, by replacing the NA's in the y matrix with 0's and setting an initial value for sigmaeps. However, chains for a number of parameters don't converge. I'm not sure whether I need to run for a very high number of iterations or whether my data are just not suited to obtaining all these estimates. But, I will try scaling back on the parameters to null models, like you suggest and see if the intercept estimates are reasonable and go from there. Also, that's a good suggestion to try in another program and I may try that as well.

Best,
Valerie

messages.subject: RE: help: N-mixture model, informative priors on detection
parts:
Dear Valerie,

just to make sure I understand: you replaced the missing responses with zeroes solely in desperation to see whether the model would run with balanced data, right ? Because obviously this will not give you the correct parameter estimates anymore.

And: what do you mean by "high number of iterations" ? Be warned, 100,000 may well be short for such models.

One advantage of JAGS is that you can easily run it in parallel (for instance, using the R package jagsUI). This may cut by a factor of about 2.5 your waiting time (with 3 chains). Note that you can also run OpenBUGS and WinBUGS in parallel, using a function written by Mathias Tobler and distributed on this list a while ago (have to check the archives).

Best regards  --- Marc
From: hmec...@googlegroups.com [hmec...@googlegroups.com] on behalf of Valerie Steen [valeri...@gmail.com]
Sent: 27 June 2016 20:26
To: hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology
Subject: Re: help: N-mixture model, informative priors on detection

Dear Marc,

Thanks much for the response.

I had the model without the detection component running (i.e. the zero-inflation binomial model and the poisson model). I actually finally had success getting the full model to run, by replacing the NA's in the y matrix with 0's and setting an initial value for sigmaeps. However, chains for a number of parameters don't converge. I'm not sure whether I need to run for a very high number of iterations or whether my data are just not suited to obtaining all these estimates. But, I will try scaling back on the parameters to null models, like you suggest and see if the intercept estimates are reasonable and go from there. Also, that's a good suggestion to try in another program and I may try that as well.

Best,
Valerie

On Monday, June 27, 2016 at 9:10:52 AM UTC-6, marc.kery wrote:

Dear Valerie,

 

Have you had these problems with (much) simpler versions of this model ? Did the Null model run (i.e., where there is an intercept only for the zero-inflation and abundance parts) ? Remember rule # 1: start with a simple model and make it more complex progressively.

 

Also, it is a good idea to throw a problem at two or more of the available BUGS software, i.e., in your case, also WinBUGS and JAGS. Sometimes a model runs in one and not the other and in the very least, the error messages may be complementary.

 

Best regards  -- Marc

Betreff: help: N-mixture model, informative priors on detection

 

Hi all,

 

In OpenBUGS (using R2OpenBUGS - although I've tried debugging directly in OpenBUGS as well) I get error: "something went wrong in procedure Poisson in module MathRandnum". I am trying to model wetland selection by migrating shorebirds. Most wetlands have 2 surveys (some 3, some 1), however the abundance of shorebirds is highly dynamic and shorebirds turnover between surveys. Thus, I put survey date (julian.z) as a covariate on abundance. Also, many 0's in the data (thus zero-inflation in model) and the data holds little information to derive detection estimates. Thus, I use estimates on detection from another study as informative priors on p (by vegetation class, i.e., light vegetative cover, medium cover, and heavy cover). Also, surveys of wetlands are spatially grouped in townships, thus the zero-inflation model and abundance model have a random effect term for township. I am wondering if anyone can spot the error (I've been debugging this for a while, but am pretty limited in my skills with this type of model and seem to be at that limit) and any help would be much appreciated! 

 

Also, the ymult matrix deals with na's in the y matrix for wetland reps with missing surveys. Na's in the y matrix are 0's in the ymult matrix, creating p effective (p.eff) of 0. 

 

BUGS model and full data are attached.

 

Example of the y data 

237 0  0 NA

238 0  0 NA

239 0  0 NA

240 0  0 NA

241 0  0 NA

242 0  0 NA

243 0  0 NA

244 0 NA NA

245 0  0 NA

246 0 NA NA

247 0 NA NA

248 2  0 NA

 

load("datax.Nmix.RData")

library(R2OpenBUGS)

 

sink("BUGS\\zip.Nmix.modelOnP.txt")

cat("

    model{

 

    #priors for zero-inflation

    a~dnorm(0, 0.44)

    

    # priors for poisson model

    for(k in 1:6){ 

    b[k]~dnorm(0, 0.01)

    }

   

    #priors for detection model

    d.int~dnorm(0,0.44)

    d[1]<-logit(mean.d1)

    mean.d1 ~dbeta(12.3,3.27)

    d[2]<-logit(mean.d2)

    mean.d2 ~dbeta(12,12)

    d[3]<-logit(mean.d3)

    mean.d3 ~dbeta(9.9,89.1)

    

    # random effects

    for(j in 1:nTC){

    rz1[j]~dnorm(0, 1)

    ry1[j]~dnorm(0, 1)

    }

       

    sigmaz1~dunif(0, 12) 

    sigmay1~dunif(0, 12) 

    sigmaeps~dunif(0, 12)

    

    for(w in 1:nW){   #loop over wetlands

    

    #zero-inflation

    z[w]~dbern(pz[w])  

    logit(pz[w]) <- a + sigmaz1*rz1[TC[w]]

     eps[w] ~ dnorm(0,1)

    

    for(t in 1:T){ #loop over the reps within each site/wetland

 

    N[w,t]~dpois(mu[w,t])

    mu[w,t]<- (1-z[w])*lambda[w,t]

    lambda[w,t] <- exp(max(min(eta[w,t],50),-10))

    eta[w,t] <- b[1] + b[2]*crop.z[w] + b[3]*julian.z[w,t] + b[4]*pow(julian.z[w,t],2) + b[5]*pow(julian.z[w,t],3) + b[6]*peri.l.z[w,t] + sigmay1*ry1[TC[w]] + sigmaeps*eps[w] 

    

    y[w,t]~dbin(p.eff[w,t],N[w,t])

    p.eff[w,t] <- (p[w,t])*(y.mult[w,t])

    logit(p[w,t]) <- d.int + d[1]*veg.1[w,t]+ d[2]*veg.2[w,t] + d[3]*veg.3[w,t] 

    }#

    }

    } #model

    ",fill = TRUE)

sink()

 

bugsworkingdir <- file.path(getwd(), "BUGS")

 

parameters <- c("a", "b","d","sigmaz1","sigmay1","sigmaeps") 

 

inits <- function() list(a=runif(1, -1, 1), b=runif(6, -1, 1),

                         sigmaz1=runif(1, 0.5, 2), sigmay1=runif(1, 0.5, 2),

                         z=as.numeric(rowSums(datax$y,na.rm=T)==0),N=datax$y+1)

mod.zip.Nmix <- bugs(datax, inits= inits, parameters,

             model.file="zip.Nmix.modelOnP.txt", n.chains=2, n.iter=100, 

             n.burnin=2, n.thin=1, debug=TRUE,

             working.directory=bugsworkingdir)

Hi Marc,

Well, I also included a matrix that indicated with 0's the NA's in the y matrix. Multiplying those together produced 'p.eff' (p effective), so while the regression for p produced estimates of p where there were no corresponding y data, 'p.eff' became the intermediary in the binomial model  y~(p.eff, N). This approach was recommended to me by someone to deal with the NA's and seemed reasonable. So, I hope it's doing what I think it's doing.

Yeah, I guess I may be far short of the number of iterations needed, in that case. I'll look into the parallel processing options. 

Thanks very much for the help, I really appreciate it!!
